subject.title: Google Chat: agent-to-agent (bot↔bot) conversation doesn't work — a Chat app doesn't receive messages from another Chat app (same setup works on Discord)

question: Should OpenClaw handle this Google Chat limitation with a docs-only clarification for now, or sponsor a channel-independent A2A bridge for logical agent mentions?
rationale: Current code can only act after Google Chat sends an inbound event, while a bridge would create new cross-agent delivery semantics outside the transport and needs maintainer intent for safety, UX, and validation scope.

options.title: Document Limitation Now
options.body: Add a Google Chat and bot-loop/multi-agent docs caveat that `allowBots` only applies to delivered events, and track bridge design separately after live proof.

options.title: Design Explicit Bridge
options.body: Define an opt-in internal route through existing sessions_send/A2A machinery with loop, access, attribution, and live Google Chat proof requirements.

options.title: Wait For Live Repro
options.body: Keep the issue open until a maintainer or operator runs a two-Chat-app Workspace proof before deciding docs or bridge scope.

recommendation.title: Document Limitation Now
recommendation.body: Add a Google Chat and bot-loop/multi-agent docs caveat that `allowBots` only applies to delivered events, and track bridge design separately after live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice spans bot-loop protection, sessions_send/A2A behavior, and product-level channel semantics, all areas with strong recent history from this owner candidate.
